          Milan 3-1 Inter Stats: Moreira Inspires Rossoneri to Derby della Madonnina Victory
        
      
                          
                      Oct 31, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Two assists and a goal from Diego Moreira helped Milan to a derby win. Re-live this Serie A game with our Milan vs Inter stats page.
Diego Moreira scored a glorious free-kick and provided two assists as Milan halted Inter‘s unbeaten start to the Serie A season, winning 3-1 in Saturday's Derby della Madonnina.
The Belgium international only needed 10 minutes to tee up goals for Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot, as Ruben Amorim's team came flying out of the traps at San Siro.
And though Alessandro Bastoni‘s first goal in 20 derby appearances got Inter back into the contest midway through the first half, more Moreira magic put the game beyond them.
Moreira's wonderful dead-ball strike in the 43rd minute restored Milan's two-goal cushion, one they would not relinquish as Inter were held at arm's length in the second half.

Back in the lineup after missing Wednesday's 4-2 defeat to Bologna due to injury, Moreira only needed four minutes to make his mark. Having hit the byline on the right, he cut back and floated a left-footed cross towards Pulisic, who nodded into the bottom-left corner.

The Rossoneri did not have to wait long for their second goal, and it came straight from the training ground as Moreira fired a low corner into Rabiot, whose deft chip clipped the far post on its way in.

Inter halved the arrears through a set-piece goal of their own in the 22nd minute, with Bastoni heading home after Hakan Çalhanoglu‘s corner was glanced on by Manuel Akanji, and only an incredible reaction stop from Mike Maignan prevented Djed Spence from levelling soon afterwards.
But Moreira ensured the Rossoneri went into half-time with a two-goal lead, as the 22-year-old curled a delightful, left-footed free-kick beyond Josep Martínez from 25 yards out.

Given a torrid time by Moreira throughout the first half, it was something of a surprise to see Carlos Augusto emerge for the second period, and he could not make the most of a headed chance in the 56th minute.

Cristian Chivu's side briefly had hope of getting back within one when referee Marco Guida pointed to the spot for an apparent handball by Mario Gila. However, a VAR review quickly let the Spaniard off the hook, as replays showed Henrikh Mkhitaryan‘s cross hit him in the chest.
From that moment on, a blocked volley from Ange-Yoan Bonny was the sum of Inter's attacking efforts, with the final whistle prompting raucous celebrations from those in red and black.
Few derbies in world football have featured as many legends of the game as this one, and on the biggest stage of all, Moreira announced himself with a memorable display.

Having set up two quickfire goals to set Milan on the path to victory, the winger confidently took the ball off Pulisic and Luka Modric to score just the third direct free-kick by a Rossoneri player in the Derby della Madonnina since Opta data collection began in 2004-05.
Andrea Pirlo previously scored a free-kick against the Nerazzurri in a Serie A matchup in December 2007, while Theo Hernandez did so in the Supercoppa Italiana in January 2025.
Moreira's performance lit up San Siro, an iconic venue on which the clock is ticking, after Milan and Inter announced plans for a new joint home, the Generali Stadium, this week.

But he was not the only Milan player to offer an important contribution. Rabiot has now scored or assisted in each of his last five Serie A matches (four goals, two assists), making him only the third midfielder to achieve that feat for Milan since the start of 2004-05, after Kaka and Calhanoglu.

Milan have now won three straight Serie A games against their rivals for the first time since Carlo Ancelotti oversaw four consecutive victories between 2002 and 2004, and across all competitions, they are unbeaten in eight against the Nerazzurri (W6 D2).
